To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CPL-1 enzyme has been overproduces in Escherichi coli, the secondary structure has been studied by circular dichroisn, the conformational change induced by choline has been detected by circular dichroison, the conformation of the CPL-1 lyoszyme is similar to the one of hen egg white lysozyme and the conformation of CPL-1 is compatible with the one predicted by secondary structure prediction.

the lysozymes coded by bacteriophages are the most promising enzymes for the development of new antimicrobials, and that choline is the most effective inhibitor of the pneumococci lysozymes, including that coded by phage Cp- 1, and that the binding site of the enzyme for this molecule has been localized.

the CPL-1 lytic enzyme, coded by the pneumo-coccal phage CP-1, has been overproduces in Escherichiacoli under the control of modified lactose promoter, and that the CPL- 1 secondary structure has been determined by circular dichroisim.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional characterization of a novel lysozyme that is coded by the pneumcoccal phage Cp-I and that is able to recognize the pneumococci cell wall.
the characterization, at the molecular level, of the structural determinants involved in the recognition of pneumococcal substrates by the CPL-1 lytic enzyme.
a structural study of a lysozyme from the bacteriophage Cp-1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CPL-1 is an alpha-helical, beta-sheet and beta-turn protein with a secondary structure that is sensitive to choline and to the presence of the substrate.
choline is able to induce a conformational change in the CPL-1 lyase which, in turn, affects the enzyme activity.
the choline molecule induces a change in the conformation of the CPL-1 lytic enzyme, thus preventing its binding to the substrate and the subsequent cleavage of the peptidoglycan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CPL-1 lytic activity is regulated by choline, which is a structural component of the pneumococci cell wall, and that the choline binding to the enzyme is associated to a conformational change of the protein.
the CPL-1 lytic activity is regulated by a choline-mediated conformational change of the enzyme.

, although the primary sequence of the CPL-1 lytic enzyme is similar to that of the pneumococci lysozyme, the CPL-1 enzyme is not able to hydrolyze the pneumocococcal cell walls, but it is able to hydrolyse the pneumocococal teichoic and the lipoteichoic acid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CPL-1 is a lysozyme of the C-type family that is characterized by a high degree of sequence identity with the human C-type lysozyme.

the CPL-1 lytic activity is finely tuned by the presence of choline, which induces a reversible conformational change in the protein, thus providing an additional level of control in the lytic process.
the lysozymes of phages Cp-1 and Cp-2 are the first examples of enzymes with a dual specificity, i.e. the ability to hydrolyze both the pneumococci cell wall and the bacterial DNA.
